correctness.rationale: For 1<t<2, 0<s<1, ts<1, 0<p<1, T=g_{s,p} o f_t has outer slope ts<1 and inner slope R=t(1-sp)/(1-p). The fixed inner barrier a=p(1-s)/(t(1-sp)-(1-p)) is interior exactly p<p_c. For R<=2 the inner core [a,1-a] is invariant with constant slope ±R, giving log R. For R>2 it has two disjoint inverse branches with contraction 1/R and full two-shift repeller; cylinder lengths yield (1-2a)(2/R)^n and dimension log2/log R, outside attracts to zero. At p>=p_c the image enters a monotone absorbing half interval, so entropy vanishes. The R=2 and p=p_c boundaries are separated. I independently evaluated exact rational thresholds and core widths at p=1/10,1/5,7/10,8/9,9/10 when t=9/5,s=1/2; they match p_*=2/11,p_c=8/9. The source proof, not these samples, covers all parameters.
